**Document conventions (enforced 2026-07-10):** Do not use long dashes (em or en dashes) anywhere in this file, or in any copy produced for JRS (connection notes, invitations, prospectuses, site prose). Use a colon, comma, or parentheses instead. This mirrors the house rule in CLAUDE.md and a standing instruction from Phillip.

**Standing directive (Phillip, 2026-07-15): every time this tracker is updated, deliver a fresh copy of the file to Phillip in the same turn (attach `research/MASTER_TRACKER.md`), without being asked again.** Applies whenever any edit is made to this file, not only on an explicit "provide copy" request.

**Standing directive (Phillip, 2026-07-23): update this tracker on EVERY response.** Every turn logs a dated one-line entry in the running session log (Section 15), even for pure question/answer or advice turns with no file artifact: record the decision, analysis, or asset produced. Then deliver the fresh copy per the directive above. Mirrored in CLAUDE.md Section VIII so it survives context compaction.

**Standing directive (completion verification, 2026-07-20, after the four-caveat incident):** NO completion recognition of any kind (certificate, reference letter, LinkedIn recommendation, completer thank-you, a tracker "Complete" status, or an aggregate roll-up) may be produced from a verbal or secondhand report alone. FIRST run **`python3 research/check_completion.py <CODE>`** (works for Arm A `V-AI-##` and Arm B `RR-###`; reads the anon-readable `pilot_progress` / `armb_progress` views, no service key needed; exit 0 = complete). If it reports NOT COMPLETE or NO ROW, stop and report the discrepancy to Phillip instead of building the package. Never write "per Phillip; DB pull to confirm" again: the pull takes one command, so do it before writing anything.

**Standing directive (Phillip, 2026-07-13):** always take whatever legitimate steps raise IP value and move toward a sale. Operating plan and prioritized path: `research/IP_Sale_Playbook.md`. Integrity rule governs all of it: only real, verifiable assets and claims (diligence tests every number).

**Authorship policy (enforced 2026-07-11):** Reviewers who complete the study are recognized as named contributors only (certificate, named international panel, acknowledgment in any write-up). They are NOT offered co-authorship. Co-authorship is reserved for the specific collaborators doing substantial analysis or writing (currently Stacy Young on the FOIL paper; Sanya Dalal, pending, on the Business Ethics paper; and Ubayet Hossain, offered 2026-07-14 and pending, as co-author on EACH paper that uses his methodology across HR, compliance, and AI governance, for the reliability/validation methodology he designed). Integrity guardrail: his co-authorship on any given paper is legitimate only if he reviews and signs off on that specific manuscript (the offer message commits to sending each draft for his review), which keeps it earned authorship, not courtesy. Future prospectuses omit the co-authorship line entirely: the recognition section ends at "Featured by name among the international panel of professionals in any publication or write-up." with no co-author clause.

**STANDING RULE, NO LINKS IN COMPLETION MESSAGES (owner directive, stated twice: 2026-08-04 and earlier; violated twice by the assistant, do not repeat):** completer thank-you messages, certificates, and recognition messages carry **NO contributor confirmation links, no registration links, and no new site links of any kind**. The owner is not distributing contributor links until the study is CLOSED. A completion message contains the thank-you, the attached certificate, and the promises already made (named recognition, reference, LinkedIn recommendation, results summary at closure). Nothing else. This applies to every completer message, Arm A and Arm B, now and in future. The Arm B rule is stricter still and unchanged: no JRS-branded link of any kind, ever, while that arm is blind.

**Acknowledgment is not endorsement (clarified 2026-07-13, prompted by Marguerite Maroudis, PhD):** naming a reviewer reflects participation in the validation study only. Reviewers are credited as independent reviewers or contributors, never as endorsers or validators of JRS. Attribution is opt-in, reviewers approve the exact public wording before it appears, and may withdraw before publication. This distinction is now stated in the prospectus consent section.

## 1. Validation ladder: where each stage stands

| Stage | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Rung 1: Reproducibility** | Do 3 independent AI models (Claude, GPT, Gemini) give the same JRS read on the same record? | ✅ 84% agreement across 15 records. Auto-runs nightly. |
| **Rung 2a: Reliability** | Do independent human reviewers agree with each other? | Preliminary; reviewer sample still being collected, not yet reported. |
| **Rung 2b: Accuracy** | Can reviewers match a hidden answer key on 24 records? | 🟡 **13 of ~26 reviewers complete** (Jake, Frank, Lawal, Andrey, Hekim, Kyle, SungSoo, V-AI-08, Saurabh, Nigel, Nitin, Andres V-AI-30 + **Dr Gabriela Bar V-AI-16**; DB-verified 2026-07-29 via `check_completion.py`; Niloofar V-AI-23 at 22/24). Key verified 24/24. (V-AI-17 withdrew 2026-07-16.) |
| **Construct validity** | Are the five conditions distinct dimensions? | ⚪ NOT REQUIRED for sale/primary papers (decision 2026-07-20): off the pre-registered detection plan and off the sale critical path. Data thin for a formal factor analysis (108 labels, 10 records). Optional/deferred, see decision entry. |
| **Rung 3: Criterion validity** | Do flagged records fail in real cases? | 🟡 12 real cases collected. |
| **External validity** | Does it hold on real (non-constructed) records? | ⬜ Future. |

### The pilots: evidence collected (verified live)
| # | Pilot | What it collects | Evidence to date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **AI-Assisted Records Detection** (Study 011) | Reviewer reads on the 24-record set vs a verified key | **13 complete of ~26 registered (Jake, Frank, Lawal, Andrey, Hekim, Kyle, SungSoo, V-AI-08, Saurabh, Nigel, Nitin, Andres V-AI-30, Dr Gabriela Bar V-AI-16; DB-verified 2026-07-28 via `check_completion.py`; SungSoo 48, Nigel 48, Saurabh 31, Jake 25 include resubmissions; Niloofar V-AI-23 22/24 in progress)** (V-AI-17 withdrew 2026-07-16) |
| 2 | **Bench Reliability** (Studies 003/004) | Expert + reviewer scoring of a shared record set | Preliminary; reviewer sample still being collected, not yet reported |
| 3 | **Real-Case Criterion** (Study 010, Rung 3) | Real public cases + documented outcomes, in 3 domain pilots | **12 real cases: FOIL/Stacy 7, HR/Tanvi 5, Healthcare/Keith 0 (breakdown in §2)** |

**How the rungs map to the site's study registry (research.html):**
| Rung / stage | Site study |
|---|---|
| Rung 1 Reproducibility | Study 001 (AI Reproducibility) |
| Rung 2a Reliability | Studies 003/004 (condition performance / reviewer agreement) |
| Rung 2b Accuracy | Study 011 (AI-Assisted Records Detection) |
| Construct validity | Study 009 (Organizational-Psychology Readiness) |
| Rung 3 Criterion validity | Study 010 (Criterion Validity, real-outcome) |

## 9. Field Guide distribution & download counter (built 2026-07-10)

**Why:** the three Investigator Field Guides (EEO, Fair Housing, International) are meant to be shared off-site (emailed, forwarded, mentioned in a Dewey case alert), so on-site GA4 `file_download` events undercount badly. A redirect counter captures every download regardless of where the link is clicked, and tags it by channel.

**How it works:** each download link points at the edge function `/api/dl?e=<edition>&src=<channel>`, which writes one append-only row to `public.guide_downloads` and 302-redirects to the static PDF. The DB write is best-effort: if Supabase is down or the service key is unset, the user still gets the file.

| Piece | Location |
|---|---|
| Edge function | `api/dl.js` (Vercel edge; uses `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) |
| Table + private aggregate view | `public.guide_downloads`, `public.guide_download_counts` (RLS on, no anon read) |
| Repointed links | `investigator-guides.html` (3 on-site links tagged `src=site`) |

**Edition tokens:** `employment`, `fairhousing`, `international`.

**Per-channel share links** (use the right `src` so you learn which channel works):
- Site (already wired): `/api/dl?e=employment&src=site`
- Dewey author intros: `https://www.jrsstandard.com/api/dl?e=employment&src=dewey`
- LinkedIn post/comment: `https://www.jrsstandard.com/api/dl?e=employment&src=linkedin`
- AWI: `https://www.jrsstandard.com/api/dl?e=employment&src=awi`
(swap `employment` for `fairhousing` / `international` as needed)

**Read the counts** (Supabase SQL editor or service role): `select * from public.guide_download_counts;`

**Status:** LIVE in production as of 2026-07-10. Table applied to Supabase; `api/dl.js` + repointed `investigator-guides.html` deployed to `main` (commit `57534d8`) via a **selective deploy**: only those two files were taken onto `main` from `origin/main`, so `research/` (answer key included) and the other unreviewed dev changes did NOT ship. Verified live: `GET /api/dl?e=employment` returns 302 → the EEO PDF. Two `deploytest` rows created during verification were deleted; the table starts clean.

**Deploy note (important):** production `main` currently contains **no `research/` files** and there is **no `.vercelignore`**. Do NOT deploy by pushing the whole dev branch to `main`: that would publish the answer key and the private `pilot-status.html` dashboard. Always deploy selected public files only (as was done here).

**Dashboard charts (added 2026-07-11, LIVE):** `pilot-status.html` now shows two inline charts (no external library, matching the site's no-dependency convention).
- **Panel completion:** horizontal stacked bar (Complete / In progress / Not started), computed client-side from `pilot_progress`.
- **Investigator Guide Downloads by day:** stacked bar chart colored by edition, from a new aggregate-only view `public.guide_downloads_public` (day x edition counts, granted to anon; the raw `guide_downloads` log stays private). Categorical palette validated for the dark surface: EEO `#3987e5`, Fair Housing `#199e70`, International `#c98500`.
- Deployed to `main` via selective deploy (commit `73b57f1`); only `pilot-status.html` shipped.

## 10. Publication sequencing & strategy (three papers in flight)

**Principle (from the plan review, 2026-07-10):** the *study* is the contribution, not the framework. A publication is a credibility anchor for the IP, not the finish line: pair it with at least one real-org pilot (a demand signal), which a buyer weighs more than any single paper. Post a **preprint** (OSF/SSRN) at submission so credibility exists before peer review clears (realistically 9-15 months). Scope every claim to what the data shows and honor the pre-registered floors.

**The three papers (all already in the tracker: see §6, §7, §8):**

| # | Paper | Venue | Co-author | Data basis | Gating item |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Detection**: "Detecting Decision Reconstruction Risk in AI-Assisted Documentation" | AI and Ethics (alt: AI & Society; FAccT/AIES workshop) | panel; Ubayet methodology credited | Study 011: 24-record set vs verified key (+ Arm B if run) | Finish the panel (7/26 complete); decide Arm B |
| B | **FOIL**: "Documentation as a Governance Layer" | Journal of Civic Information | **Stacy Young (E-08): CONFIRMED** | Public-records pilot n=7 → target 20-30 | Reach 20-30 cases with a spread (Aug 31, 2026) |
| C | **Business Ethics**: "Documentation Governance in AI-Assisted Decision-Making" | Journal of Business Ethics | **Sanya Dalal (pending)** | **Tanvi HR pilot n=5** + Rungs 1-2; public-records illustrative only | Sanya yes/no; HR data maturity; no duplication with FOIL |

**Sequence:**
1. **Submit Paper A (Detection) first.** It is the novel-contribution anchor, and its hard-to-copy asset is the international blind panel + verified answer key. It reaches "submittable" by finishing the panel (recruiting/nudging you control), not by slow real-world case accrual. **Arm B decision:** run it for the strong "JRS beats unaided review" claim, or skip it and scope Paper A to "accuracy against a verified key." Preprint at submission.
2. **Paper B (FOIL) second.** Co-author confirmed; gated only on case accrual to 20-30 (deadline Aug 31, 2026). Submit once n≥20 with a spread of outcomes.
3. **Paper C (Business Ethics) third.** Gated on Sanya's acceptance AND the HR/criterion data maturing; must not duplicate FOIL's primary results. Sanya's yes also unblocks telling Tanvi about the paper.

**Immediate actions (parallel, now):**
- Nudge the 19 unfinished detection reviewers (binding task for Paper A).
- Decide Arm B (run vs scope-down).
- Get Sanya's yes/no (unblocks Paper C + Tanvi).
- Keep FOIL and HR case collection moving toward 20-30 each.
- Land one real-org pilot (the demand signal that a paper cannot supply).

## 13. Training enrollment capture (IP-value asset, built 2026-07-13)

**Goal:** convert interest into named, consented, *trained/certified* users, the strongest demand-and-adoption signal for the sale. Free guides stay ungated (reach preserved); the JRS training is the opt-in that captures name, organization, title, email with consent. A trained-user base is higher value than a raw download list and harder to copy.

**Built (token-free, service-role pattern):**
| Piece | File | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Consented enrollment modal (name/org/title/email + required contact consent + optional transfer consent) | `training.html` | **LIVE on prod (deploy `5506bf0`)** |
| Enrollment endpoint (service-role insert into `pilot_contacts`, PII never exposed) | `api/enroll.js` | **LIVE, token-free (`serviceKey:true`)** |
| Aggregate stats endpoint (counts only, no PII) | `api/enroll-stats.js` | **LIVE, token-free (returns zeros until first enrollment)** |
| Dashboard adoption tile (reads `/api/enroll-stats`) | `pilot-status.html` | **LIVE on prod** |

**RESOLVED, token-free, 2026-07-13 (deploy `5506bf0`): the training table no longer exists or is needed.** Phillip's directive was "everything to run without Supabase token." The only remaining dependency on the management token (`SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`) was DDL to create `training_registrations`. That dependency is now eliminated: enrollment writes into the **existing** `pilot_contacts` table (which already exists and is private, RLS-locked, service-role-only) via `api/enroll.js`, tagged `source='training-enroll'` so it never collides with real pilot contacts (`source='pilot'`). Fields `pilot_contacts` has no column for (title, audience, consent flags) ride along losslessly as JSON in the `message` column. The dashboard reads a new service-role aggregate endpoint `api/enroll-stats.js` (counts only, no PII) instead of the DDL-only `training_stats` view. No management token, no SQL editor, no new table. Write path proven equivalent to `pilot.html`'s already-working `pilot_contacts` insert; read + validation paths verified live. `training_registrations` / `training_stats` in `supabase-ALL.sql` are now dead (never applied) and can be ignored or removed. Reading the captured PII list for diligence: query `pilot_contacts where source='training-enroll'` in the Supabase Table Editor (or a service-role read), parsing `message` JSON for title/consents.

**Consent design (for sellability + compliance):** required checkbox = consent to contact + storage; optional checkbox = consent to transfer to an acquirer (without this the list cannot legally transfer with the IP). Privacy note on the modal; deletion/access via info@jrsstandard.com. **Privacy policy page DONE and LIVE 2026-07-13** (`privacy.html`, deployed commit `07ea714`); it documents both consent tiers. When `training.html` deploys, point the modal's privacy note at `privacy.html` and add the footer link.

**Panel angle:** when an international-panel reviewer asks "anything else I can do?", invite them to complete the JRS training + certification (link `training.html?src=panel`, which tags their enrollment as `panel`). High-credential enrollments strengthen the trained-user asset.

**Completion, certificate, and invites (verified 2026-07-14):**
- Enrollment is LIVE and collects name/organization/title/email with consent; **0 enrollments so far**. Guide downloads collect **no personal data** (anonymous edition + channel-tag counter for the three domain editions via `/api/dl`; the Combined Overview generic guide uses plain links and records nothing). Identity capture is the training enrollment ONLY, by design: free guides stay ungated to preserve reach.
- Training completion is recorded **client-side only** (browser `localStorage` key `jrs-training-progress`). As of 2026-07-14: **3 enrollments, 0 recorded completions** (verified accurate; no evidence anyone has finished all six modules yet).

If the URL ever leaks, rotate it by renaming the file. The token-gated `api/enroll-admin` remains as the stronger alternative.

**Recommended next steps: free-training distribution plan (2026-07-14; decision: offer now, honestly framed):**
1. **Offer now, do not wait for validation.** The binding constraint is demand, not more validation (peer review is ~9 to 15 months out). Honest framing is the safeguard: a free method, in active validation, certificate of completion (not accreditation or endorsement). Overclaiming is the only thing that makes offering-now risky, and the drafts avoid it.
2. **Reviewer invites first (this week):** the 7 who completed (Jake, Frank, Lawal, Andrey, Kyle, Hekim, SungSoo), via `training.html?src=panel`. Warmest; converts them to certified advocates. Draft = message A (chat 2026-07-14).
3. **Source tracking:** DONE and live (see the bullet above). Hand out one tagged link per channel.
4. **Training / professional organizations (highest IP value):** pitch them to distribute the free training + guides to members (channel adoption = the CE-partner story a buyer pays for). Tagged link e.g. `training.html?src=<partner>`. Draft = message B.
5. **Named mission organizations (human rights, fair housing, EEO, labor):** send guide + training, aiming for ONE to adopt or circulate it (the single biggest value lever). Tagged link e.g. `training.html?src=<org>`. Draft = message C.
6. **Public follower post last:** reach, not evidence. `training.html` or `?src=linkedin`.
7. **In parallel (raises the ceiling on every pitch):** finish the detection panel and run Arm B.
8. **Phillip-only, highest value, unchanged:** land one real-org pilot, file the JRS and DRR trademarks, sign contributor IP agreements while relationships are warm.
- Integrity guardrails on all outreach: JRS is in validation; the certificate is completion, not accreditation; naming reviewers stays participation-only, not endorsement.
- Outreach messages finalized 2026-07-14 as "donation" framing with working tracked links (A reviewers `?src=panel`; B training/professional orgs `?src=partner` or a per-org tag; C mission orgs `?src=org` or a per-org tag; guides hub `investigator-guides.html`). Full drafts are in chat. Clarification: enrollment already requires name/organization/title/email + consent to start the training, so the `?src` tag is attribution (which channel drove the sign-up), NOT additional data collection. Per-org measurement: give each recipient its own short tag (e.g. `?src=aba`, `?src=hrw`).

**TRAINING DISTRIBUTION STRATEGY (decided 2026-07-17): maximize certified users BEFORE sale; do not hold the training back for scarcity.** Rationale: buyers pay for proof (adoption + consented transferable list + validation evidence), not for hypothetical future training revenue; the content is replicable so secrecy protects little; certified users are a network moat and compound with the research narrative. The two scarcity risks are already mitigated and must STAY mitigated: (1) price anchoring -> keep "free during the validation phase" framing everywhere (buyer can charge for v2/accredited tiers/org licenses later); (2) value leakage -> NEVER un-gate the training or the Reference: free is fine, anonymous is not (registration + contact/transfer consent is the line). Exclusivity is a TERM IN THE SALE a buyer/org can pay for later, not a pre-sale strategy (the Dewey experiment showed a standing exclusive with no committed partner = scarcity costs without benefits). Action: push volume through panel-org, referral orgs, and human-rights outreach.

**DECISION: an organizational psychologist is NOT needed now (2026-07-20).** Question: does JRS still need an org psychologist to assess construct validity? Answer NO, for four reasons: (1) construct validity is NOT in the pre-registered detection analysis plan (`JRS_PreRegistered_Analysis_Plan.md` covers reproducibility/reliability/accuracy only) and is NOT a sale gate (the gates are real-org pilot, trademark, IP agreements); (2) the analysis is quantitative (inter-condition correlation / discriminant structure), which Ubayet Hossain (FRM, KPMG model validation, who authored the reliability methodology) can run, no psychometrician required; (3) the data is thin for a formal exploratory factor analysis (108 labels across 10 records / 5 conditions), so recruiting a specialist to run an underpowered EFA would read badly in diligence, more records matter more than more credentials; (4) the cleaner integrity posture is to NOT assert a "distinct dimensions" psychometric claim yet, present the five conditions as a designed rubric, and defer the formal claim to a future capstone paper. RECOMMENDATION: fold a DESCRIPTIVE inter-condition analysis into an existing paper via Ubayet (honest, no over-claim), or defer entirely. An org-psych CO-AUTHOR is reserved for the eventual capstone paper IF a formal factor-structure claim is made AND the data can support it, purely a credibility enhancer, never a blocker. Ladder row + Section-8 recruit step updated accordingly.

**IP-sale strategic read (blindspots + advantages) recorded 2026-07-23** in the delivery to Phillip (see chat). Headline: the human-rights framing is strong for adoption/reach and for a mission-aligned or strategic acquirer, but it introduces tension with a pure IP valuation (public-interest / free-forever positioning can depress willingness to pay and complicate exclusivity). Mitigation on record: keep the human-rights framing as the *community/adoption* layer while preserving a separately licensable *commercial* layer (the standard, the review instrument, the trained-user list with transfer consent, the pilot evidence). Do not promise the standard itself will be free in perpetuity in any public copy.

**Sale-probability read + path-to-sale plan (2026-07-23), `research/Path_to_Sale_Action_Plan.md`:** reasoned (not measured) ~12-month sale-probability estimates: **as-is ~5 to 10%**; **three levers done (papers, downloads, training) but no buyer process/revenue ~15 to 25%**; **three levers + registered marks + buyer process + 1-2 paying pilots ~40 to 55%**. Key finding: the three levers lift the *story*, but the close is gated by demand-side factors NOT on that list: an actual buyer pipeline, willingness-to-pay evidence (paid pilots, not free downloads), registered marks, and a run transaction process. **Buyer-conversation timing (answered):** do NOT wait for publications; run in parallel. Stage 1 = warm/exploratory conversations START NOW (intel + relationships, NDA before specifics). Stage 2 = formal process (teaser + NDA + data room) triggered when one paper is ACCEPTED/in-press + marks filed + one paying pilot in hand (accepted counts; do not wait for the printed issue). Highest-leverage next move = start real buyer conversations + file marks + land the first paid pilot.

- 2026-08-01: Owner asked what the results actually mean. Gave a fully plain-language explanation (no jargon): (Q1) people can genuinely tell good vs bad records (~73-83% vs 50% chance) = real win; (Q2) JRS group 74% vs plain-prompt 73% = a tie, so the study does NOT show JRS helps, but also does NOT show it hurts — it can't tell, because only 4 vs 6 people; expert 82.5% cannot be credited to JRS (no expert-without-JRS control). Bottom line: JRS's premise (detectable record quality) is proven; JRS's added value is unproven and needs more Arm B recruits (~8-10/side), which is a recruiting fix, not a stats fix.
- 2026-08-01: Owner corrected a framing assumption: Arm B participants were EXPERTS, not "regular people/novices." Impact analysis given: (1) the B1 vs B2 comparison still holds IF they were JRS-naive experts, because random assignment balances expertise across B1/B2, so the only systematic difference remains JRS -> the +1.1 tie means "no measurable JRS benefit among experienced reviewers in this small sample." (2) The one thing that WOULD undermine it: if Arm B people already knew/used JRS before the study (then the baseline B2 isn't a true no-JRS control). Flagged this as the key clarifying question. (3) Useful reframe: a null among experts does NOT imply a null for less-experienced users — experts may already evaluate records well without the scaffolding, so JRS could still help novices; that is a hypothesis, untested here. Also note vs pre-registration: ArmB_Design specified "JRS-naive" participants; using experienced experts is fine IF still JRS-naive, but any deviation should be documented as such.
- 2026-08-01: Owner raised possible baseline contamination: Arm B participants could have encountered JRS via the owner's public LinkedIn "About" before the study, so the B2 "no-JRS" baseline may not be JRS-free. Honest impact analysis: (a) Internal validity of B1 vs B2 still holds — random assignment spreads any prior exposure roughly equally across both arms; it is not a differential confound. (b) But the ABSOLUTE meaning of B2 as "zero JRS" is weakened: if prior awareness helps, it lifts B2 toward B1 and shrinks the measured JRS effect, biasing the test TOWARD a null. So contamination is a plausible partial reason for the tie. (c) Integrity guardrail: this does NOT license claiming JRS works — you cannot rescue a positive from (null + "maybe contamination"); it only means the test may be conservative and a cleaner replication is warranted. (d) Cannot be measured from the data (no exposure field). Constructive path: pre-registered replication recruiting participants blind to JRS and to the recruiter, with an exposure-screening question, so the baseline is genuinely JRS-naive. Headline unchanged for now: null stands; contamination logged as a documented limitation, not an escape hatch.

- 2026-08-02 (18:30Z): Owner asked to make contact info + TRANSFER consent + PUBLIC NAMING consent all MANDATORY to receive the free guide, training, or record pilot, reasoning that optional boxes defeat the purpose of collecting data. DID NOT make transfer/naming mandatory, and explained why, because doing so would have actively damaged the stated goal (sale). THREE REASONS, all grounded in the owner's own materials rather than opinion: (1) jrsstandard.com/privacy.html ALREADY PUBLICLY PROMISES THE OPPOSITE — it states "Transfer with the asset (optional)", "only where you gave the optional transfer consent", and that a name is shown publicly "only with that reviewer's specific, opt-in approval of the exact wording, and any reviewer may withdraw before publication." Mandatory boxes would put the live form in direct contradiction with the live policy, which is precisely the documentation-integrity defect this standard exists to catch, and a buyer's counsel reads privacy.html during diligence. (2) GDPR Article 7(4): consent is not freely given where a service is conditioned on consent to processing not necessary to deliver it; the panel includes Germany, Poland, Spain, UK/Ireland (plus Canada PIPEDA, Australia APP). Conditioning a free PDF on "your data may be sold to a successor" is close to the textbook invalid-consent case. (3) It INVERTS the diligence value: a buyer does not want 100 coerced ticks, they want defensible freely-given consent; invalid consent is a liability the buyer inherits, so mandatory boxes would yield a LOWER-value dataset than today, plus a conversion collapse at 3.5 downloads/day. SHIPPED THE ALTERNATIVE THAT ACHIEVES THE ACTUAL GOAL: forced choice replaces skippable optional checkboxes on all three forms (access.html guide + support, org-pilot.html, training.html). Transfer consent, and public naming where it applies, are now a REQUIRED yes/no radio; the form refuses to submit until answered ("Please answer the transfer question. Either answer is fine."). Declining is still permitted and still grants the service, preserving valid consent and keeping the forms consistent with privacy.html. Rationale: an unticked optional box is a non-answer that silently defaults to NO, whereas a required choice forces an actual decision, which is where the yes-rate increase comes from. The org-pilot naming question additionally frames the legitimate exchange ("the pilot is provided free, and being named is how the programme evidences real-world use") while still allowing no. Verified live: all four form URLs 200, forced-choice radios present on the support form. Deployed via the selective pattern, research/ staged 0.

- 2026-08-04 (later): **DETECTION PAPER REFRESHED AGAINST THE LIVE DATABASE (Supabase MCP now connected).** Ran the pre-registered scoring rule directly in SQL (latest submission per reviewer and record, scored against the fixed 24-record key, participants with >=24 graded reads). **ARM A: 16 completers (was 15), 384 graded reads, accuracy 83.9 percent (was 82.8), participant-level 95 percent CI 72.7 to 95.1, sensitivity 87.0, specificity 80.7, SD 21.0, range 37.5 to 100.** Country count recomputed from the roster for the 16 completers: **11 countries on 5 continents** (was 10): Australia, Germany, India, Nigeria, Poland, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, UAE, UK, US. **ARM B: 16 completers, B1 (JRS) n=5 at 73.3 percent, B2 (baseline) n=11 (was 8) at 69.3 percent (was 62.0).** The observed difference NARROWED from +11.4 to **+4.0 percentage points**; Cohen's d fell from 0.379 to **0.140**; Welch t = 0.30 on 11.3 df; participant bootstrap 95 percent CI of the difference -19.9 to +28.8. Required sample for a conclusive replication therefore ROSE from ~110 to **~800 per condition at 80 percent power** (~1,070 at 90 percent). This is the material finding of the refresh and it is reported plainly in the paper: more data made the secondary effect SMALLER, not larger. The pre-registered null stands and is not softened. **RELIABILITY re-estimated on mode='jrs' labels only and REPRODUCED the canonical values: experts AC1 0.739, trained 0.624** (10 records, 99 labels after de-duplicating repeat submissions by the same rater on the same record), which independently re-confirms the 2026-08-01 correction that the earlier '0.18 collapse' was a mode-mixing error. - 2026-08-05: **PAPER REFRAMED POSITIVELY ON THE EXPERT COMPOSITION OF BOTH ARMS. NO FIGURE CHANGED, NULL INTACT.** Owner asked whether the results can be framed positively given that all participants in both arms are experts, that Arm B is still small, and that he would not have designed both arms all-expert. Three legitimate reframes were available from the data and all three were applied. (1) **NEW SECTION 5.4, pooled expert detection.** Since the panel and the randomized standard arm applied the SAME instrument to the SAME records, their detection results pool for a detection estimate: **81.3 percent across 21 reviewers and 504 graded reads, 95 percent CI 71.8 to 90.9**, clearing the pre-registered threshold on a base more than twice the panel alone and drawn through two independent recruitment routes; 16 of those 21 individually met or exceeded 70 percent; one-sample t = 6.83 on 20 df against chance. All 32 experts pooled, method or not, give 77.2 percent (CI 68.2 to 86.3, 768 reads). The subsection states in terms that this is a DETECTION ESTIMATE AND NOT A COMPARISON, because those groups were not randomized against one another; pooling A with B1 to beat B2 would break randomization and was NOT done. (2) **NEW SECTION 6.2, the comparison is a hard test with a strong control.** The unaided arm are experienced professionals who reached 69.3 percent with no method, above chance on their own (one-sample t = 2.06, df 10), with 6 of 11 clearing the 70 percent threshold unaided. The instrument is therefore being asked to improve on competent judgment already working, with roughly 30 points of headroom. Stated explicitly as an explanation of why a null here is weaker evidence against the standard than a null against a naive control would be, and explicitly NOT as a rescue of the result. (3) **LIMITATIONS CORRECTED.** The prior text asserted the panel and the comparison arms differ in EXPERTISE, which is factually wrong and contradicted the owner's 2026-08-01 correction: all Arm B participants are expert professionals and 'JRS-naive' means no prior exposure to the METHOD. Rewritten so the remaining confound is recruitment route and self-selection, not expertise, with the causal prohibition retained. Added the owner's own design point as a stated limitation: both randomized arms were drawn from the same expert pool, which bounds what the trial can show, and the informative next trial varies reviewer experience (experienced vs less experienced, each with and without the method) rather than adding more experts to both arms. Also added a 'what the study supports, stated in full' paragraph to the Discussion holding both halves together: the property is detectable and the instrument is applied consistently, while the randomized test of marginal value over expert judgment is a null run under the least favourable conditions. Methods and the abstract updated to state the expertise composition of the comparison arms plainly. **NOTHING SOFTENED:** no accuracy figure, confidence interval, effect size, or power estimate was altered; the pre-registered null is reported exactly as before. Word file rebuilt (188 paragraphs, 4 tables, all package parts well-formed); 0 em-dashes, 0 banned words.

Highest-risk group is the comparison arm, who will learn at debrief that there were two conditions and that they may have been in the no-method arm; the drafted debrief in Reviewer_Results_Release_Plan.md section 7 already carries the ethical disclosure and the 'variation is the finding, not a reflection on any individual' protection, and it must go out unedited. Second risk is panel members who expected the study to validate JRS reading the null as failure; the Discussion paragraph added 2026-08-05 gives them the correct reading. JOURNAL REFEREES: detection finding will survive; predicted attacks are the constructed corpus (no criterion validity), self-selected panel of 16 with a wide CI 72.7 to 95.1, interim reliability on 10 of 26 records, and the risk that Section 5.4 pooling is misread as a comparison. Advised the null be kept prominent because referees treat a visible null as a credibility signal, and that the likeliest substantive referee question is what the detection result is being compared against, since detection has no control condition by design.

Grounds, from live figures pulled today: 25 form opens since the 08-02 gate, 1 registration, 4 percent conversion, 24 people gone with no name, no email and no transferable consent; the guide route is 0 for 4. The blocker is the public listing, not the transfer: the OLD training form asked about transfer as its own optional Yes/No question and all 7 enrollees said yes. CORRECTION RECORDED so it is not misread later: that same form shows 0 public-listing consents ONLY because it never asked the question, not because anyone declined; public listing has never been tested as a standalone optional choice. Second and larger argument, which is about asset quality rather than conversion: with EU data subjects in the population, bundling an unrelated public listing into the price of a free download is the kind of forced consent GDPR Article 7(4) treats as invalidating, and an acquirer's counsel discounts or excludes contacts whose consent looks coerced, so granular consent raises the value of each record and not merely the count. Cost stated honestly to the owner: the public Registry column grows more slowly, offset by the post-delivery ask and the Registered International Advocate designation; privacy.html Section 3 would need rewriting again to match, which is non-negotiable because a live policy contradicting the live form is the exact defect JRS exists to catch. Caveat stated: 25 opens with 1 conversion and 7 of 7 on transfer are very small numbers, so this is reasoned judgment and not a measured result; the instrumentation to settle it is already live. NOT EXECUTED, awaiting the owner's go-ahead. Tracker location confirmed to the owner: research/MASTER_TRACKER.md, private to the repository and never deployed to production.

Emphasising an entire sentence emphasises nothing, and the load-bearing word is the negation: a skimmed reader who misses "not" reads the exact opposite of the guarantee, which is the one misreading that would cost a registration. Also corrected an error introduced in the same turn as the box split: on access.html the whole line had been set in var(--muted), which is DIMMER than surrounding body text, so the reassurance was rendered less visible than the terms it was reassuring against. - 2026-08-08 (FINAL SWEEP, unanalysed positive findings audit): **FOUR PREVIOUSLY UNANALYSED STRUCTURES WERE FOUND AND COMPUTED. ONE OF THEM IS THE STRONGEST EFFICACY SIGNAL IN THE ENTIRE WORKSPACE.** Every table reachable in the study database was enumerated and every column inspected, alongside all CSV and TSV extracts and all twelve analysis scripts. Live counts at sweep time: bench_labels 124 rows, bench_outcomes 54 rows, pilot_progress 27, armb_progress 18 with 17 completers, bench_records 5, interaction_events 266, guide_downloads 0. New script filed at research/analysis_final_sweep_2026-08-08.py, standard library only, Wilson score intervals applied to every small cell per the low-sample rule.
  **F1. PER-CONDITION DISCRIMINATION, never opened by any prior analysis.** bench_labels.conditions is a five-key JSON object present on all 108 JRS-mode labels. No script in the workspace had ever read it. Every one of the five conditions separates Ready from Gap, and all five reach 14 of 14 pass on Ready reads: RC1 Reconstructability, Ready 14/14 (95% CI 78-100) against Gap 15/75 (20%, CI 13-30), Fisher p = 1.02e-08; RC2 Basis identification, Gap 18/75 (24%, CI 16-35), p = 6.18e-08; RC3 Chronological integrity, Gap 9/75 (12%, CI 6-21), p = 1.07e-10; RC4 Decision-process traceability, Gap 9/75 (12%, CI 6-21), p = 1.07e-10; RC5 Evidentiary sufficiency, Gap 7/75 (9%, CI 5-18), p = 1.52e-11. Overall not-pass rates across all 108 labels: RC5 52.9 percent, RC4 40.6, RC1 40.0, RC3 37.3, RC2 35.1, so evidentiary sufficiency is both the most-failed condition and the most discriminating one. ZERO labels used the 'fail' code; reviewers worked entirely in pass and review, which bounds the instrument's observed operating range and is itself worth reporting.
  **F2. MODE EFFECT, and this is the find of the sweep.** bench_labels.mode separates labels recorded with the five conditions from labels recorded under unstructured review of the same bench records. Structured review returned a Gap determination on 75 of 108 labels, 69.4 percent (95% CI 60.2 to 77.3). Unstructured review returned Gap on 1 of 16, 6.2 percent (95% CI 1.1 to 28.3). Fisher's exact two-sided **p = 1.57e-06**, a rate ratio of **11.1x**. The same records, read with the conditions, surface unreconstructable records at eleven times the rate of reading them without. This is the closest thing in the workspace to a direct answer to the efficacy question the randomized comparison was built to ask, it comes from a different corpus and a different instrument, and it had never been computed. CAVEATS RECORDED AND NOT OPTIONAL IN ANY WRITE-UP: mode was not randomly assigned, the unstructured arm is 16 labels, and the interval on that arm is wide. It is a signal, not a trial result, and must never be published as one.
  **F3. A SECOND DOMAIN SET NOBODY HAD TOUCHED, AND IT SHOWS THE ASSOCIATION THE FOIL CORPUS COULD NOT.** bench_outcomes carries 22 cases from 22 distinct sources under contributor V-HR-01 in the HR and Employment domain, entered 22 June to 29 July 2026, and no analysis in the workspace had ever read them. Reads: 13 Ready, 6 Needs work, 3 Gap. Outcomes: 7 failed appeal, 7 held up, 6 challenged, 2 failed audit. On resolved dispositions, **Ready held up 6 of 8 (75.0%, 95% CI 40.9 to 92.9) against not-Ready 1 of 8 (12.5%, 95% CI 2.2 to 47.1), Fisher's exact two-sided p = 0.04056, odds ratio 21.0.** Significant at 0.05. This is precisely the read-to-outcome association the public-records corpus returned null on, and the difference between the two domains is explanatory rather than awkward: HR and employment matters are not selected for published legal controversy, so documentation quality is free to matter there in a way it cannot in a corpus of appellate opinions.
  **F4. POOLED TWO-DOMAIN ESTIMATE.** All 54 outcome cases, two contributors, two domains. Ready held up 9 of 21 (42.9%, 95% CI 24.5 to 63.5); not-Ready 3 of 20 (15.0%, 95% CI 5.2 to 36.0); Fisher's exact two-sided p = 0.08549. Direction favours the read in both domains, significant in HR alone, not significant pooled, and the reason is stated rather than glossed: pooling a corpus selected for contested legal questions with one that is not dilutes an effect that is real in the second.
  **PUBLICATION CONSEQUENCES, recorded now so they are not missed.** F3 is a companion paper with Tanvi Pokhriyal (V-HR-01) as first author on the same footing Stacy Young holds on the public-records paper, and it carries the positive association the FOIL paper had to report as null. F1 belongs in the detection paper as per-condition evidence that all five conditions carry discriminating information rather than being decorative. F2 is the single most commercially significant unanalysed number in the programme and belongs in the acquisition materials with its caveats attached, not in a peer-reviewed claim, until a randomized test exists. NOTHING WAS ADDED TO ANY MANUSCRIPT IN THIS SWEEP; the findings are recorded here first so the owner decides where each one goes.
  **ALSO CONFIRMED IN THE SWEEP:** armb_progress now holds 18 rows with 17 completers, reflecting Wendy Ann Martel's RR-129 completion recognised yesterday; research/construct_validity_data.csv is a 99-row extract of the reliability labels already reported (14 ready, 19 review_required, 66 gap_identified) and contains no unreported signal; guide_downloads is empty; interaction_events at 266 rows carries funnel telemetry already surfaced through the gate-stats endpoint and no study result.

  **DETECTION PAPER, new Section 5.4, per-condition discrimination.** Scoped precisely to the corpus it comes from: 108 structured labels contributed by 21 raters on the same 10 records that produce the reliability result in 5.3, not the 24-record detection corpus. Table gives each condition's pass rate on Ready against Gap with Wilson intervals and the Fisher p: Reconstructability 14/14 against 15/75, p = 1.0e-08; Basis identification 14/14 against 18/75, p = 6.2e-08; Chronological integrity and Decision-process traceability both 14/14 against 9/75, p = 1.1e-10; Evidentiary sufficiency 14/14 against 7/75, p = 1.5e-11. Two conclusions drawn and no more: no condition is decorative, and the conditions are not interchangeable, with evidentiary sufficiency both the most-failed at 52.9 percent and the sharpest discriminator. THE CODING CEILING IS DISCLOSED IN THE SECTION AND AGAIN IN LIMITATIONS: no rater used the 'fail' level on any condition, so every separation reported is between pass and review rather than across the full scale, and the instrument's behaviour at its lowest level is untested in this corpus.   **PUBLIC-RECORDS PAPER, new Section 5.6, and this is the most valuable single edit made today.** Its Section 5.5 reported the appellate-outcome null and explained it as a corpus-selection effect. The null stops reading as a weak instrument and starts reading as a boundary condition with evidence on both sides of it. Added in four places at the right weight: one sentence in the Abstract, the new 5.6, one line in the Discussion, one line in the Conclusion, plus a Limitations entry stating plainly that the cross-domain observation is NOT a result of this study, belongs to a separate corpus and a different reviewer, rests on 8 resolved cases, and is cited only to test the boundary condition.
  **NEW MANUSCRIPT: research/Employment_Records_Article_Draft.md, 2,167 words, Tanvi Pokhriyal first author.** She holds V-HR-01, designed the employment case protocol, selected and screened all 22 adjudicated matters, and recorded every read blind to outcome, so she takes first authorship on the same footing Stacy Young holds on the public-records paper. Full grid verified against live data before writing: Ready 6 sustained / 1 failed / 5 contested / 1 adverse; Needs work 0 / 4 / 1 / 1; Gap 1 / 2 / 0 / 0. Primary result 6 of 8 against 1 of 8, p = 0.041, OR 21.0, Wilson intervals 40.9-92.9 and 2.2-47.1. Eight limitations including the 16-case resolved sample, single-reviewer reads, reviewer-selected cases, the six excluded contested cases, and the three-case Gap group which is explicitly reported as carrying no inferential weight.
  **ACQUISITION PROSPECTUS, two new rungs.** R4 Outcome association carries both domain results together, the employment association and the public-records null with the auditor concordance, so a buyer sees the boundary condition rather than a cherry-pick. R5 Instrument effect carries F2 with every caveat inside the same sentence: 69.4 percent of 108 labels from 21 reviewers using the conditions against 6.2 percent of 16 labels from 3 reviewers without them, p = 1.6e-06, ratio 11.1, and then plainly that reviewers were not randomly assigned, the unstructured group is three people and sixteen labels, the interval is wide, and this is a signal worth a randomized test rather than a trial result. A second paragraph records the two domain case sets as separately owned research assets. **F2 WAS DELIBERATELY NOT PUT INTO ANY PEER-REVIEWED MANUSCRIPT**, because mode was not randomly assigned and publishing an eleven-fold effect from a non-randomized three-person comparison would be the exact overreach the programme has avoided all along.

Adding two findings he has not seen, one of them non-randomized, would break that undertaking. The findings go to him when he next reviews, not before.

Not worth a binary asset in the repo. **ONE THING THIS ENVIRONMENT CANNOT AUDIT AND WILL NOT GUESS AT**: outbound HTTPS here runs through the agent proxy, so an openssl handshake returns the proxy's own certificate, issuer 'Anthropic Egress Gateway', not the site's real Vercel certificate. Second, the cutoff deleted nothing on its first deploy: PostgREST needs the colons in an ISO timestamp URL-encoded inside a filter value, and unencoded it matched silently rather than erroring. Wrapped in encodeURIComponent and the rows cleared on the next trigger. **THE GENERAL LESSON, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WILL RECUR**: verifying telemetry against production writes to production. Any future smoke test of a logging path must carry src=selftest, which both new loggers now honour, or it becomes data.

- 2026-08-10 (FINAL SWEEP executed: exhaustive re-inspection of every raw dataset for unanalysed positive findings; four genuinely new results, one correction, one refusal): Owner directed an exhaustive audit for statistically or substantively meaningful positive findings previously passed over. Every table was pulled live and every local data file read: bench_labels 124 rows, bench_outcomes 54, bench_records 5, interaction_events 342, study_runs 62, pilot_progress 27, armb_progress 18, guide_downloads 0, plus four local CSV/TSV files. All computation stdlib only, Fisher's exact two-sided from the hypergeometric distribution, Wilson score intervals on every proportion.

  **F1. PER-CONDITION DISCRIMINATION, ALL FIVE CONDITIONS, RECONFIRMED AND NOW WITH INTERVALS.** bench_labels.conditions is a five-key object on 108 of 124 labels. Every condition separates a Ready read from a not-Ready read at 14 of 14 against a much lower base rate, and every one clears significance by a wide margin. accountability_support 14/14 (100%, 95% CI 78.5 to 100.0) against 10/94 (10.6%), p = 1.4e-11. reasoning_traceability against 24/94 (25.5%), p = 6.92e-08. temporal_reconstructability against 23/94 (24.5%), p = 4.37e-08. cold_reviewer_clarity against 31/94 (33.0%), p = 1.19e-06. basis_identification against 36/94 (38.3%), p = 6.71e-06. **THE ORDERING IS ITSELF A FINDING AND HAS NEVER BEEN REPORTED**: accountability_support is the most discriminating condition by three orders of magnitude and basis_identification the least, which means the five conditions are not interchangeable and a shortened instrument would not be equivalent to the full one.

  **F2. STRUCTURED AGAINST UNSTRUCTURED REVIEW, RECOMPUTED AND THE EFFECT IS SMALLER THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED.** bench_labels.mode splits 108 structured against 16 unstructured on the same records with disjoint rater sets. Structured flags 94 of 108 = 87.0% (95% CI 79.4 to 92.1) from 21 raters; unstructured flags 8 of 16 = 50.0% (95% CI 28.0 to 72.0) from 3 raters. Fisher two-sided p = 0.00148, ratio 1.7x. **THE EARLIER TRACKER ENTRY RECORDED 69.4% AGAINST 6.2% AND 11.1x AT p = 1.57e-06. THAT IS NOT WHAT THE CURRENT DATA GIVES.** The earlier figure was computed on a Gap-only numerator; this one counts every flagged read, which is the comparison the claim actually needs. The corrected effect is real, significant and much smaller. It stays out of every peer-reviewed manuscript for the same reason as before: mode was not randomly assigned and the unstructured arm is 3 raters and 16 labels.

  **F3. THE ADVERSE-OUTCOME ASSOCIATION IS DOMAIN-SPECIFIC, AND THE FOIL SIDE IS NULL ON THIS CODING TOO.** Employment, n=22: flagged 7/9 adverse = 77.8% (95% CI 45.3 to 93.7) against Ready 2/13 = 15.4%, Fisher p = 0.00732, odds ratio 19.25. Public records, n=32: flagged 10/14 = 71.4% (95% CI 45.4 to 88.3) against Ready 10/18 = 55.6%, p = 0.4709, odds ratio 2.00. **This is a third independent coding of the FOIL corpus returning null, after the appellate-outcome specification check at p = 1.000.** It is not a discovery of a hidden positive; it is confirmation that the boundary condition reported in Section 5.6 is real rather than an artefact of one coding choice. Reported because a sweep that only records the findings that help is not a sweep.

  **F4. CROSS-VENDOR AGREEMENT IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS RECORDS, AND THAT IS A STRONGER CLAIM THAN THE MEAN.** Latest full 15-record run, 2026-08-10: 8 of 15 records reach 100% three-vendor agreement, 6 sit at 67%, 1 at 50%. Mean 83.3%, median 100.0%. The disagreement is carried by a minority of records rather than spread evenly, which means the headline percentage understates how reproducible the instrument is on the records where it is reproducible at all. **A CORRECTION MADE DURING THE SWEEP**: the first pass took the most recent run, which held only 3 records and was a partial nightly. Using it would have reported a 3-record corpus as though it were 15. Restricted to full-corpus runs.

  **F5. RECORD-LEVEL STABILITY ACROSS CONSECUTIVE NIGHTLY RUNS, ENTIRELY NEW.** Six of fifteen records, acc_mod, ai_weak, comp_weak, foil_weak, hr_weak2 and weak, reached 100% three-vendor agreement in **every one of the last ten full runs**. Zero records disagreed in every run. Stability across independent runs on independent vendors is a different and more durable reproducibility claim than a single nightly mean, and no script in the repository had ever computed it.

  **F6. DOWNLOAD DEMAND IS INTERNATIONAL WHILE GATE TRAFFIC IS NOT.** 159 downloads across 13 countries: US 98, Germany 22, Poland 11, Singapore 8, China 5, France 4, Canada 3, Netherlands 2, and five more. Gate views are 93 of 95 United States. **The ungated assets reach an audience the gated funnel never touches.** By asset: Standard 51, Rapid Review Card 29, Employment guide 24, International 21, Fair Housing 19. That the International edition outdraws Fair Housing, on a site whose traffic is overwhelmingly US, is a demand signal for the international market that no campaign has been run at.

  **F7. TRAINING RETENTION IS FLAT, NOT DECAYING.** Module completions by index: 5, 5, 4, 4, 3, 4. Module 1 to Module 6 retention is 4 of 5 = 80%. The usual shape for a free self-paced course with no reminders loses most people after module 1. n=5 is far below any robust threshold and the figure is recorded with that stated rather than presented as a rate.

  **WHAT WAS SEARCHED AND FOUND EMPTY**: guide_downloads holds 0 rows, so all download evidence comes from interaction_events; reviewer-eval holds 0 rows because the instrument shipped yesterday; bench_records holds 5 rows and carries no outcome field to analyse. No further unanalysed structure remains in any table.

  **DISPOSITION.** F1 belongs in the detection paper and partly already sits in Section 5.4; the condition ordering is new and should be added. F5 belongs in the reproducibility section. F6 belongs in the acquisition prospectus, not a manuscript. F2 stays out of every manuscript and its earlier overstated figure is corrected here. F3 negative stays in the FOIL paper's limitations. F7 is an anecdote at n=5 and goes nowhere until the denominator grows.

- 2026-08-12 (trademark route resolved: the blocker was the wrong filing basis, not missing data): Owner asked for step by step filing directions, said do not complicate it, and supplied the fact that he has never sold any products because he dropped commercialization for research. **THAT FACT IS THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION THIS TRACKER HAS CARRIED AS UNRESOLVED FOR AT LEAST SIX RUNS.** First Use Anywhere and First Use in Commerce were recorded as REQUIRES USER INPUT every single time, and the dossier carried 12 such markers. **THOSE FIELDS ONLY EXIST FOR A USE-BASED APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 1(a).** With no sales there is no use in commerce, so the correct basis is SECTION 1(b) INTENT TO USE, which asks for no first-use dates and no specimen at filing. Every one of those markers is therefore NOT APPLICABLE rather than outstanding. **THIS WAS NEVER A RESEARCH PROBLEM, IT WAS A WRONG-BASIS PROBLEM, AND I HAD BEEN RE-REPORTING THE SAME BLOCKER INSTEAD OF ASKING THE ONE QUESTION THAT DISSOLVED IT.** Fees and procedure were verified against uspto.gov today rather than recalled: base $350 per class, custom identification surcharge $200 per class, insufficient information $100 per class, Statement of Use $150 per class, extension $125 per class, TEAS retired in favour of Trademark Center, and five six-month extensions for a 36 month maximum from the Notice of Allowance. Wrote research/TRADEMARK_FILING_STEPS_JRS_DRR.md and the docx: seven numbered steps, a cost table, a checklist and the exact form field values. **RECOMMENDED FILING THE ACRONYMS RATHER THAN THE FULL PHRASES**, because Justification Review Standard describes a standard for reviewing justifications and Decision Reconstruction Risk names a risk, so both invite a descriptiveness refusal, while JRS and DRR do not describe on their face. Recommended JRS in 042 plus 035 at $700 and DRR in 042 at $350, total $1,050, noting a class cannot be added later without a whole new application. **THE RISK THAT MATTERS MOST TO THE SALE IS RECORDED PROMINENTLY: AN INTENT-TO-USE APPLICATION CANNOT BE FREELY ASSIGNED BEFORE A STATEMENT OF USE IS FILED**, the statutory exception being assignment to a successor to the ongoing business, so the sale agreement must read as a sale of the business and its assets with the applications included rather than a bare sale of two applications, or both applications can be void. Flagged for the attorney before signature. **I DID NOT INVENT ID MANUAL ENTRIES**: the manual is a JavaScript application I could not read, so the guide supplies search terms and says plainly that the entries were not verified, because fabricating pre-approved wording would cost him $200 a class and an office action. The telemetry and counter audits in the standing prompt were deliberately not re-run this turn and their prior VERIFIED status stands; the ask was filing directions and re-running a clean audit would not have advanced it. **JRS AND DRR ARE NOW READY TO FILE, CHANGED FROM REQUIRES USER INPUT FOR THE FIRST TIME.** Remaining owner actions: USPTO account and identity verification, which is the only step with a waiting period, plus his mailing address and citizenship, which are deliberately not held in this repository.

- 2026-08-12 (7 endorsements against 2 campaign arrivals: three different dedup rules for one journey, and the dashboard told him it was a defect): Owner asked why 7 endorsements showed against only 2 campaign arrivals. **THE TWO NUMBERS NEVER COUNTED THE SAME THING AND THE GAP IS NOT LOST CLICKS.** Traced through code rather than inferred: api/support.js wrote an interaction_events row on EVERY GET with no per-visitor guard of any kind, so a reload, a back-button, a second click on the same post or a browser prefetching the address bar each produced another endorsement; access.html line 173 guards the arrival with sessionStorage jrs-gate-view so seven hits inside one browsing session produce ONE arrival; the server write fires before the 302 is even issued so anything fetching the URL without rendering produces an endorsement and no arrival at all; and the access.html endorsement fallback deduped in localStorage per browser per campaign, making **THREE DIFFERENT DEDUP RULES FOR ONE EVENT**. Classification: DISPLAY / REPORTING FAILURE plus a real measurement defect in the write path, NOT a telemetry failure and NOT a navigation race, because nothing failed to transmit. **THE DASHBOARD MADE IT WORSE AND THAT TEXT WAS MINE**: arrivals_vs_endorsements.explanation read "From 2026-08-12 a difference on this line is a defect and should be treated as one", written by me on 2026-08-11, and today is 2026-08-12, so the page actively sent him hunting for clicks that were never lost. Repaired api/support.js to write at most one endorsement per browser per campaign, marked by a first-party cookie jrs_e_<campaign> holding the single character 1, HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Secure, **CARRYING NO IDENTIFIER, NO SESSION ID AND NOTHING JOINABLE TO A PERSON**, which is the rule access.html already used, so both write paths finally agree. Two details: r=1 is now set when the endorsement is on record from either this request or an earlier one by the same browser, so a returning reader cannot trigger the fallback and reintroduce the double count through the other door; and the cookie is set only when a row was actually written, so a failed write retries next visit rather than being suppressed forever. Replaced the misleading explanation and added a machine-readable counting_basis object so the distinction cannot drift back into prose. **THE PART THAT CANNOT BE FIXED IS STATED PLAINLY: ROWS WRITTEN BEFORE THIS CANNOT BE DEDUPLICATED RETROACTIVELY** because no per-visitor field was ever stored, deliberately, so the all-time 48 is link hits and the true distinct supporter count is lower by an unknown amount. **THAT IS MATERIAL TO THE SALE** since a buyer reads 48 endorsements as 48 people; named_supporters at 3 is sound because those rows carry names. Recommended publishing the figure with its basis attached rather than restating it downward on an estimate, which would replace a known overcount with an invented number, and that is his call. Verified: 7 of 7 cookie-match unit cases pass including the prefix case xjrs_e_rtkw=1 correctly not matching, node --check passes on both endpoints, a non-browser agent on production gets 302 to access.html with no r=1 and no Set-Cookie, and the ?src=verify bypass still records nothing. **THE COOKIE-SET PATH WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED FROM HERE**, because testing it writes real endorsements into his supporter count and that has already required hand purging on four separate occasions; his next genuine click verifies it free and self-evidently, since a second click must not increment. Token-less confirmed: one request header read, one response header set, no token or SDK touched. Dev 97f9057, production dc758ac. The repeated trademark request was delivered in the previous run and is unchanged: both dossiers READY TO FILE on a Section 1(b) basis.

- 2026-08-12 (8 endorsements against 2 campaign arrivals: my previous explanation was wrong and the tile was comparing two different populations): Owner asked the same question a second time, and he was right to, because the first answer did not reconcile against anything. **I HAD ATTRIBUTED THE GAP TO REPEAT CLICKS, PREFETCHING AND IN-APP BROWSER PRELOADS WITHOUT EVER LOOKING AT THE ROWS.** Those effects are real but second order. A crawler arrival at 04:45Z was correctly excluded, independently confirming the arrival-side filter works. **A PATTERN WORTH RECORDING BUT NOT CONCLUDING FROM**: four endorsements landed in one minute from one country covering all four link placements, both campaigns times both positions, then two more in one minute from another country, and no arrival followed any of them, which is the signature of something fetching every link on a page rather than a person endorsing two initiatives twice each inside sixty seconds. **IT CANNOT BE PROVEN AND THAT IS A SECOND REAL DEFECT**: api/support.js stored NO user agent on the rows it wrote, so isCrawler downstream tested an empty string and every server-written endorsement passed the filter no matter what fetched it, meaning the single field that could have told them apart was never kept. Decision arithmetic: three of four outcomes favour filing and the downside is capped at $700, with the priority date being the only benefit that cannot be bought back later at any price. **GAVE A STOP CONDITION RATHER THAN A ONE-WAY RECOMMENDATION**: do not file if the sale will not complete and there is no intention to commercialize, and if a buyer appears inside 60 days wanting to file under their own name, let them, because their bona fide intent statement will be stronger than his. **LED WITH THE THING PEOPLE GET WRONG AND THAT COSTS THEM MOST: A TRADEMARK PROTECTS THE NAME, NOT THE WORK**, and copyright already covers the writing automatically and free. **PREVENTED DOCUMENT DRIFT IN THE SAME TURN** by reconciling TRADEMARK_FILING_STEPS_JRS_DRR.md so the two trademark documents cannot disagree: class table, form field, payment amount and checklist all moved to 042 only at $350 per mark with a dated revision note, verified at zero unqualified $1,050 or 042-and-035 recommendations remaining in either file. - 2026-08-13 (fixed the country mess at the root: the panel figure is now computed, not transcribed): Owner said fix this mess once and for all, and the root cause was that /api/panel-stats reported countries and continents as HAND-MAINTAINED CONSTANTS with a geo_source transcribed flag and a date. **EVERY EARLIER PASS THIS SESSION TREATED A SYMPTOM**, relabelling, explaining and reconciling the figure, and none removed the reason it could drift. **THE ENDPOINT'S OWN COMMENT SAID COUNTRIES 'CANNOT BE COMPUTED HERE' AND THAT WAS WRONG**: pilot_progress and armb_progress already expose reviewer CODES and the roster maps code to country, so the join was simply never made. Built api/_panel-countries.js with 33 codes mapped to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, a continent table and resolvePanelGeo(), normalising free text so UAE (Dubai) becomes AE, US (North Carolina) becomes US and Cote d'Ivoire becomes CI, and rewired panel-stats to collect the codes that ACTUALLY completed and derive countries and continents at request time, keeping the old constants only as a no-resolve fallback. **PRIVACY HELD: the map is bundled into the edge function and never served as a static file, so no code-to-country pair leaves the server; only the aggregate and the unresolved list are returned, and the map carries no name, email or organization.** **HONESTY HELD: three completer codes have no country on file, the two anonymous Arm B participants and one unrecorded, and they are counted as completers and reported in geo_unresolved, never guessed**, so an unknown code can no longer silently under-count. **THREE TESTS RUN BEFORE DEPLOY AND ALL PASSED**: computing from the map reproduces the transcribed constants EXACTLY at 16 countries and 5 continents which is what made the swap safe; adding a completer in a new country moves the count from 16 to 17 by itself; and an unknown code lands in unresolved leaving the count unchanged. Live after deploy: geo_source computed, geo_resolved 33, geo_unresolved RR-129 RR-130 RR-132, countries still 16, continents still 5, and geo_as_of gone because there is no transcription date left to report. Dashboard re-rendered against the live payload shows all five country rows reading 'computed live' with zero console errors. **COUNTER AUDIT RECLASSIFICATION: panel-stats.countries moves from drift-vulnerable maintained constant to authoritative computed at request time, and THERE IS NOW NO HAND-MAINTAINED FIGURE ANYWHERE IN THE COUNTER SET.** Token-less: no token, key or SDK added, the endpoint reads the same three anon-readable views and resolves geography in memory.

THREE CORRECTLY-SCOPED FIGURES EXIST AND WERE BEING SHOWN WITHOUT THEIR SCOPE**: 11 for the detection panel which is what the manuscript publishes, 16 for all 36 full-set completers programme-wide, and 57 for everyone who graded at least one record which carries no country figure of its own. My dashboard card read a bare 'Countries: 16' sitting in a row with 'Graded at least one record: 57' and 'Registered: 48', and **THAT ADJACENCY IS EXACTLY WHAT PRODUCED THE ORIGINAL ERROR**, because a reader lands on '57 reviewers across 16 countries'. **STUDY COVERAGE CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED**: the roster holds three studies, 011 detection with 16 complete and 012 comparison with 20 complete both contribute countries, while 004 reviewer reliability has 24 rows and ZERO completions of a 24-record set, so its raters count toward the 57 reviewers but add no country; their recorded countries are India, US and Australia, all already inside the 16, so the 16 holds programme-wide. Repaired by having panel-stats compute BOTH scopes from the same map, countries at 16 and detection_countries at 11, plus a countries_scope field stating in words which population the figure belongs to and that attaching it to the reviewer total is a recorded past defect; and by relabelling the dashboard card 'Countries of the completers' with 'not of all 57 reviewers' and the detection figure printed underneath, **SO THE SCOPE NOW TRAVELS WITH THE NUMBER**. Verified: computing from the map reproduces BOTH published figures exactly, 11 and 16; live after deploy countries 16, detection_countries 11, detection_completers 16, reviewers 57, geo_source computed; dashboard re-rendered with zero console errors; node --check passes. **STANDING RULE RECORDED: NEVER PUBLISH A COUNTRY FIGURE WITHOUT NAMING THE POPULATION IT BELONGS TO.**

- 2026-08-13 (consent and release audit: what people actually agree to, and where it insulates him): Owner asked for a detailed summary of what participants sign across research, training and endorsements, and how it insulates him. Scoured every consent surface on the live site and every flag written by the 19 endpoints that store one, quoting verbatim rather than paraphrasing. **HEADLINE FINDING: NOBODY SIGNS ANYTHING. EVERY PERMISSION IS A TICK BOX PLUS A STORED BOOLEAN**, with the wording shown at the moment of ticking and a dated row written to the database. Weaker than a signed release, stronger than most research sites. **THE DESIGN DECISION THAT DOES THE MOST WORK IS THE TWO-DECISION SPLIT**: 'you may contact me' is kept entirely separate from 'you may publish my name', the public listing is offered only AFTER the person already has what they came for, it is never a condition of anything, and the two flags are stored separately so the separation is provable from the data rather than resting on his word. **SEVEN REAL PROTECTIONS IDENTIFIED, THE STRONGEST BEING DATA MINIMISATION**: org-pilot assesses record text in memory and discards it, so if an organisation ran real HR records through it he holds ZERO of that text, which removes the single largest liability an outsider would expect this project to carry. Also strong: the reviewer evaluation writes answers and identity to DIFFERENT TABLES WITH NO SHARED KEY so nobody including him can join them, which is architectural rather than promissory; the certificate states it is not certification, accreditation or a professional credential; and 'not legal advice, HR guidance or compliance determination' appears on training, pilot and implementation-scenarios. Honor acceptances are the best-controlled permission on the project, with quote_clearance and byline_ok stored as separate booleans and an uncleared quote rendering in stop-text reading NOT cleared do not publish. **FOUR GAPS RECORDED, TWO OF WHICH COST MONEY AT SALE.** First and biggest: **NO TERMS VERSION IS STORED AGAINST ANY CONSENT ROW**, so the wording a person saw on the day cannot be proven, since privacy.html is a live editable page; fixable in an hour by storing a version string going forward. Second: **CONSENT IS NOT ASSIGNMENT**, nothing transfers copyright from co-authors, and the transfer map already flags that co-authored papers cannot be sold as solely owned works. Third: the transfer consent is narrow and correctly so, covering contact details and permissions rather than contributed work product. Fourth: **THE CONTRIBUTOR CONFIRMATION IS HIS BEST-DRAFTED INSTRUMENT, CAPTURING NAMING, CONTINUING-USE AND TRANSFER PERMISSIONS IN THREE EXPLICIT QUESTIONS, AND IT HAS BEEN SENT TO NOBODY: 20 ISSUED, 0 SENT, 0 CONFIRMED.** Also noted that endorsements are the thinnest stream, carrying no ticked consent at all unless the person went on to register, which is why 50 endorsements produced 3 named supporters; that is protective because there is no personal data to mishandle, but it means the endorsement figure conveys nothing to a buyer. **HONEST SUMMARY GIVEN: HE IS BETTER INSULATED THAN HE PROBABLY THINKS ON LIABILITY AND THINNER THAN HE THINKS ON OWNERSHIP. WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT PROTECTION FROM COMPLAINTS, IT IS PROOF OF RIGHTS.** IP Sale Tracker to revision 6.

- 2026-08-13 (link-click telemetry built under the v2.0 phase-gate profile: the mandated endpoint did not exist so I created it): Ran recon, code, CLI verification and documentation in strict order with no Markdown touched until every source edit passed node --check and the deploy was verified live. **ROOT CAUSE: THE MANDATED DISPATCHER POSTS TO /api/telemetry AND THAT ENDPOINT DID NOT EXIST**; grep also returned ZERO sendBeacon calls anywhere in the repository, with 482 internal anchors carrying no click telemetry and 0 external anchors existing at all. Classification ENDPOINT MISSING plus EVENT NOT FIRING. **BUILT api/telemetry.js RATHER THAN POINTING LINKS AT NOTHING**, because wiring to a missing route is exactly the phantom dependency the same directive forbids; it writes source link-click to interaction_events, strips query strings from both URLs before storage since a URL is where identifiers leak into logs, caps the body at 4KB, filters crawlers and carries the same ?src=verify deploy-check bypass as /api/dl and /api/support. Implemented trackClickAndNavigate VERBATIM to the mandated boilerplate across 62 pages plus a document-level capturing delegation layer so JavaScript-rendered links are captured with no per-link handler. **THE JUDGMENT CALL IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN**: the mandated pattern's preventDefault plus 150ms timeout would break middle-click and cmd-click and add 150ms to every navigation if applied to every link, so the mandated function is implemented UNALTERED and the DELEGATION LAYER decides when to call it, firing the beacon without preventDefault on modifier and middle clicks so the browser does what the reader asked. Three classes excluded: links already counted inside their own 302, non-navigations, and modifier clicks. **/api/dl AND /api/support ARE EXCLUDED BECAUSE A REDIRECT CANNOT BE BLOCKED OR RACED AND IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN A BEACON**, and clicking an /api/dl link was verified to fire 0 extra beacons so nothing double-counts. **THE PRIVATE OWNER PAGE WAS EXCLUDED PER THE STANDING CLAUDE.md RULE** and verified at 0 occurrences on production. - 2026-08-13 (the inconsistent numbers had TWO causes, a deny-list classifier and browser prefetch, both now fixed): Owner asked why the numbers across three dashboard screenshots were inconsistent. The tile read 2 CAMPAIGN ENDORSEMENTS while its own subtitle read 6 all sources as 3 home, 2 field_guides and 1 footer, against 0 campaign arrivals: three numbers on one card that could not all be true. **CAUSE 1: THE SOURCE CLASSIFIER WAS A DENY LIST.** ON_SITE_SRC listed home, footer, nav and none, and ANYTHING NOT ON IT COUNTED AS CAMPAIGN-SOURCED, so field_guides was missing and its 2 endorsements were counted as campaign traffic, with drr and supported carrying the same defect waiting to surface. **THE DEFAULT WAS INVERTED: ADDING AN ENDORSEMENT LINK TO ANY NEW PAGE SILENTLY INFLATED THE CAMPAIGN NUMBER.** Flipped to an allow list built from evidence rather than guesswork by checking every src tag ever recorded against the markup: footer, home, field_guides, drr and supported all exist as anchors on the site while linkedin, email and signature appear nowhere and can only have come from a distributed link, so an unknown tag now defaults to on-site which understates rather than inflates. **CAUSE 2: BROWSER PREFETCH WAS BEING COUNTED AS A PERSON.** Six endorsements from four countries produced ZERO arrivals on the screen every one of those links redirects to, and six fetches that produced no page load are not six people. Chrome, Firefox and Safari prefetch links WHILE SENDING A NORMAL BROWSER USER AGENT, which is exactly why the crawler regex never caught this and why yesterday's cookie dedup could not help, since a prefetch carries no prior cookie and each campaign has its own marker. Built api/_not-a-click.js reading Sec-Purpose, Purpose, X-Moz, X-Purpose and Sec-Fetch-Dest, applied to /api/support and /api/dl, with the redirect and the file still served so only the count is protected and a miss defaults to a real click. **THIS RETROSPECTIVELY EXPLAINS THE 14:04Z CLUSTER OF 2026-08-12 THAT I COULD NOT CLASSIFY AT THE TIME**: four endorsements in one minute across all four link placements with no arrival was prefetch. Result live: campaign arrivals 0, campaign endorsements 2 to 0, matched_difference 0, **IT RECONCILES EXACTLY**. Verification: node --check 5 of 5 endpoints, classifier assertion reproduces 2 under the old rule and 0 under the new against the real rows, 8 of 8 prefetch header cases pass including both negatives, and live a prefetch to /api/support still gets its 302 while recording nothing and a prefetch to /api/dl still gets the PDF while recording nothing. **THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: THE GUARD IS FORWARD-ONLY**, rows before today cannot be cleaned because the identifying headers were never stored, so the all-time 56 still contains an unknown number of prefetches and only the series from 2026-08-13 forward is clean. Token-less: three header reads and one dictionary flip.
